headline: Debora has declined in bathing and lower-body dressing (now moderate assist), has unsteady gait, and is avoiding showers out of fear of slipping. Her spouse and primary caregiver, Kevin, reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note matches every detail: moderate assistance, independent at last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting Debora out of the tub. Debora said she has been skipping showers because she is afraid of slipping.
items.verifier_note: The aide note matches: hands-on help getting out of the tub, and skipping showers because of fear of slipping.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches the gait findings, TUG of 19 seconds, the three recommendations, and PT twice weekly.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, Debora's spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches: Kevin's exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist updated the blister pack on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks; no recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The notes and medication record show sertraline 25 mg started on 09-13 with a PHQ-9 of 14, the blister pack updated on 09-15, and a 4-week recheck planned. The cited notes contain no recheck.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for this season (season start 2026-08-01). The most recent flu vaccine on record is 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season, and the latest on record is 2026-04-25, before the 2026-08-01 season start.

questions_for_team: Who will follow up on the equipment recommendations from OT and PT (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, front-wheeled walker, grab bars, home safety evaluation), and by when?
Can home care hours for bathing be increased, and how will Debora be kept safe and clean while she avoids showers?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and when will the team check back with him?
Has the 4-week sertraline follow-up and repeat PHQ-9 happened, and does Debora's fear of slipping or avoiding showers affect the mood assessment?
Should a flu vaccine be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) against the last IDT review date and note any gap in documentation since the prior review.
Falls and near-falls: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred while on new or changed medications (metoprolol, sertraline, albuterol).
ED visits and hospital admissions or observation stays in the window, with reasons, and whether a post-discharge follow-up occurred.

Medication changes in the window: sertraline 25 mg started 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14). Check start-date reconciliation, prescriber, any dose titration plan, and whether the follow-up mood assessment is scheduled.
Sertraline safety monitoring: bleeding risk with concurrent clopidogrel, hyponatremia signs (sodium on recent labs), GI symptoms, sleep or agitation changes, and any falls since starting.

Respiratory status for COPD/chronic bronchitis: inhaler use pattern and refill gaps (fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol started 2026-04-25), rescue inhaler frequency, oxygen use, exacerbations, steroid courses, and spirometry or pulmonary follow-up if due.

Cardiac status for ischemic heart disease: chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, metoprolol and clopidogrel and simvastatin adherence, resting heart rate and blood pressure trends, and lipid panel timing.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including orthostatic readings if dizziness or falls were reported, given metoprolol therapy.
Weight trend and BMI (obesity, BMI 30+) plus prediabetes markers: HbA1c or fasting glucose timing and results, and any nutrition or activity referrals.
Hypothyroidism monitoring: TSH timing and result against levothyroxine 0.075 mg dose, and whether levothyroxine adherence or administration timing has been addressed.
Breast cancer history (malignant neoplasm of breast, onset 2000): surveillance imaging and oncology follow-up status, and any new symptoms reported in the window.
Chronic pain and function: pain scores, analgesic use (no analgesics appear on the active list, so verify OTC or PRN use), and ADL/IADL changes including mobility, bathing, and medication management.
Cognition and mood: repeat PHQ-9 or equivalent after sertraline start, mood and sleep reports, any new cognitive concerns, and attendance at scheduled PACE center days or missed visits.
Allergy record: the allergies field is empty; confirm allergy status with the participant and update the record.
Caregiver and social situation: any change in living arrangements, caregiver strain, transportation barriers, or financial concerns since the last review.

Care-plan items due or overdue in the window: IDT goal progress, participant and family consent or care-plan signatures, transportation and home-safety reassessments, and any scheduled vaccinations or screenings.
Chronic sinusitis: symptom flares, antibiotic or steroid courses, and ENT follow-up status.
